title: Practice: estimating roots
intro: No calculator. Trap each root between two whole numbers, then judge which side it is closer to. Answers within 0.1 of the true value are accepted.

questions.prompt: Quick-fire: squares, cubes and their roots. Numbers only.
questions.explanation: Every estimate in this lesson starts from these facts. If any of them slowed you down, write out the tables of squares to $20^2$ and cubes to $10^3$ and learn them.

questions.prompt: Which of these estimates is **obviously wrong**?
hints: What is $5^2$? Is it more or less than 20?
questions.explanation: $5^2 = 25$, which is already bigger than 20, so $\sqrt{20}$ must be **less** than 5. (It is about 4.5.) The others are all sensible: $\sqrt{50}$ is just above 7, so 6.9 is a slight underestimate but close.

hints: Square (or cube) each whole number and compare with the number under the root.

questions.prompt: Estimate $\sqrt{59}$ one step at a time.
questions.scenario: Estimate $\sqrt{59}$ to 1 decimal place without a calculator.

steps.prompt: What is the largest square number **below** 59?
What is the smallest square number **above** 59?

steps.feedback: 59 is 5 below 64 but 10 above 49, so it is closer to 8.

steps.prompt: Give your estimate of $\sqrt{59}$ to 1 decimal place.
steps.hint: Try squaring 7.6 and 7.7 to see which lands nearer 59.

questions.explanation: $49 < 59 < 64$ so $7 < \sqrt{59} < 8$. 59 is closer to 64, and checking gives $7.7^2 = 59.29$, so $\sqrt{59} \approx 7.7$.

questions.prompt: Complete the table. Give each estimate to 1 decimal place.
hints: For a square root use $1, 4, 9, 16, 25, \dots$; for a cube root use $1, 8, 27, 64, 125, \dots$
The estimate must sit between the roots of the two numbers you wrote.
questions.explanation: $\sqrt{32} = 5.66\dots$, $\sqrt{75} = 8.66\dots$, $\sqrt[3]{35} = 3.27\dots$ and $\sqrt[3]{150} = 5.31\dots$ Anything within 0.1 of these is a good estimate.

questions.prompt: A square has an area of $17\ \text{cm}^2$. Estimate its side length to the nearest millimetre.
questions.explanation: Side $= \sqrt{17}$. Since $\sqrt{16} = 4$ and 17 is only just above 16, the side is just over 4 cm. $4.1^2 = 16.81$ and $4.2^2 = 17.64$, so to the nearest millimetre it is $4.1$ cm (41 mm).

questions.prompt: A cube has a volume of $70\ \text{cm}^3$. Estimate its side length to the nearest millimetre.
questions.explanation: Side $= \sqrt[3]{70}$. $64 < 70 < 125$ so the side is between 4 and 5 cm, much closer to 4. $4.1^3 = 68.9$ and $4.2^3 = 74.1$, so the side is $4.1$ cm to the nearest millimetre.

questions.prompt: $n$ is a positive integer. List every possible value of $n$, separated by commas.
hints: Cube every part of the second: $n < 8$.
questions.explanation: Squaring $2 < \sqrt{n} < 3$ gives $4 < n < 9$, so $n = 5, 6, 7, 8$. Cubing $\sqrt[3]{n} < 2$ gives $n < 8$, and $n$ is a positive integer, so $n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7$.

questions.prompt: Estimate the **negative** square root of $0.45$ to 2 decimal places.
hints: 0.45 is much closer to 0.49, so try $0.67^2$.

questions.prompt: Drag the marker to your estimate of $\sqrt[3]{-15}$.
hints: 15 is 7 away from 8 and 12 away from 27, so a little nearer $-2$.
questions.explanation: $-27 < -15 < -8$, so $-3 < \sqrt[3]{-15} < -2$. It is slightly closer to $-2$. In fact $\sqrt[3]{-15} = -2.47\dots \approx -2.5$.
